name: Executive order of April 24, 1886 adding land south of the San Juan River to the Navajo Reservation
citation: Executive order of April 24, 1886 (Royce area 658; Kappler vol. 1, p. 877)
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. It withdrew from sale and settlement all those parts of Township 29 North, Ranges 14, 15 and 16 West of the New Mexico principal meridian lying south of the San Juan River, and set them apart as an addition to the Navajo Reservation.
landTaken: None by this order: it added land. Royce records the same townships as restored to the public domain by the order of May 17, 1884.
today: No court, Commission or congressional finding about this order was located. The Navajo Commission dockets concern aboriginal title, a different event.

sources.title: Grover Cleveland, Executive Order Adding Land to Navajo Reservation (April 24, 1886)
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 920, executive order of April 24, 1886, Navaho
Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 916, executive order of May 17, 1884, Navaho

openQuestions: The order returned to the reservation townships restored to the public domain in 1884 (cession-1884-05-17-navaho); whether any of that land passed to settlers in between was not researched.
The Navajo Nation's own account of this order was not located.
